original_question: If two Artin groups of spherical type are quasi-isometric, must they be commensurable? (This is not true for right-angled Artin groups.)
target_in_paper: Problem 21.129 (I. Soroko) in the 'New Problems (21st issue, 2026)' section of arXiv:1401.0300: 'If two Artin groups of spherical type are quasi-isometric, must they be commensurable? (This is not true for right-angled Artin groups.)'
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official open problem almost verbatim: it has the correct class of groups (Artin groups of spherical type), the correct implication direction (quasi-isometric ⇒ commensurable), and it retains the paper's contextual caveat that the analogous statement fails for right-angled Artin groups.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it should define 'Artin groups of spherical type' as Artin groups associated to finite Coxeter graphs (equivalently, finite Coxeter groups).
It should define 'commensurable' explicitly: there exist finite-index subgroups of the two groups, not necessarily of the same index, that are isomorphic.
It should specify that 'quasi-isometric' is meant in the usual finitely generated-group sense, i.e. with respect to word metrics for some/equivalently any finite generating sets.
It should make the universal quantification explicit: for every pair of spherical-type Artin groups A[Γ] and A[Ω].

The parenthetical remark about right-angled Artin groups is context, not part of the formal mathematical assertion; it can be retained or omitted depending on whether one wants a pure question statement or the paper's exact flavor.
refined_question: Let A[Γ] and A[Ω] be Artin groups of spherical type, meaning that their associated Coxeter groups W[Γ] and W[Ω] are finite. If A[Γ] and A[Ω] are quasi-isometric as finitely generated groups (equivalently, with respect to word metrics coming from finite generating sets), must they be commensurable; that is, do there exist finite-index subgroups H ≤ A[Γ] and K ≤ A[Ω], not necessarily of the same index, such that H ≅ K?
justification: The draft is already essentially the exact official formulation of Problem 21.129 in arXiv:1401.0300. The only nearby paper-supplied precision needed to make it fully self-contained is the definition of commensurability, which is given immediately in Problem 21.128. Since this draft clearly targets Problem 21.129 itself, there is no narrower conjecture/theorem elsewhere in the paper to substitute for it.
